class_id: one retry key shared by two steps, so one step's failure re-runs the other
feature: scraper/src/index.ts due-step cycle (catch-up cadence keys); any branch where two steps sit behind a single isCatchUpCadenceDue / markCatchUpCadenceRan pair
symptom: A cadence key gates a whole branch but is stamped on the AND of several steps' results, so a failure in the cheap step suppresses the stamp and re-runs the EXPENSIVE step on every wake. Introduced and caught in review on 2026-09-11: the aggregator key was gated on `cgOk && fillOk`, so ONE failed row out of 231 in the issue-type fill - a single transient deadlock - left the key un-stamped and re-ran the Chittorgarh SCRAPE plus a full report fetch every 30 minutes, roughly 48 times a day against a third-party source, instead of once a day. The amplification is unbounded in time: it persists until the failing step succeeds. It was also DATE-TRIGGERED - CURRENT_YEAR is read from the clock, so on 1 Jan 2027 the report URL flips to a financial year with few rows, trips the job's own minimum-row floor, aborts, and the hammering runs for weeks with no code change at all.
first_seen: Sep 2026, PR #569. Introduced by the fix for a DIFFERENT finding in the same review (a failed fill was suppressing its own retry for a day) - the fix traded a one-day suppression for a permanent retry storm. Never reached production: caught in round 2 before merge.
fix_prs: #569 (each step gets its own cadence key and stamps on its own result; the fill is additionally gated by its own isCatchUpCadenceDue so it cannot run more often than its interval)
detection_check: scraper/tests/unit/index-issue-type-fill-wiring.test.ts - asserts ISSUE_TYPE_FILL_CADENCE_KEY exists, that `if (cgOk && fillOk)` is absent as a STATEMENT, and that the two stamps are separate. Mutation-checked: restoring the coupled key turns it red. NOT a runtime check - the cost of this class is external HTTP traffic, which no in-repo signal observes; the guard is therefore source-level and the real control is the design rule below.
rule: A cadence/retry key belongs to exactly ONE step. If two steps share a branch, they get two keys. Stamping a shared key on the AND of both results means the cheaper step's failure sets the expensive step's retry rate - and an outbound fetch against a third party is the most expensive thing in that pair.
